historic_survey.note: Named as one of two good San Francisco examples of the Streamline Moderne style, alongside the Aquatic Park Bathhouse of 1939 — a comparison the statement draws to place the single Streamline Moderne building in Duboce Triangle. Christopher VerPlanck's context statement of 2022 surveyed 552 properties in Duboce Triangle for the Duboce Triangle Neighborhood Association.

building.name: Henry Doelger Building
building.completed_conflict: The 2013 Sunset District builders context statement dates this building to 1932; the assessor dates the building on this parcel to 1940.

hook: The Henry Doelger Building of 1940, a San Francisco landmark of the Streamline Moderne.

historical_record.description: A two-storey-over-basement house clad in rustic wood siding was built at the back of this then-oversized 50-by-100-foot lot, then numbered 348 Judah Street.
The 1911 house and a one-storey outbuilding at the sidewalk were demolished to clear the site.
Henry Doelger bought the 26-by-100-foot lot to build a headquarters and sales office for his growing house-building firm.

Built 1932. Architect: Charles O. Clausen. The Henry Doelger studio: planning office, sales office, architectural studio and warehouse of builder Henry Doelger, 1932-1950; addition to the west in 1940; from here Doelger planned construction across the Sunset district and his Westlake, Daly City development.
The one-storey-with-mezzanine Art Deco headquarters of Henry Doelger Builder Inc. was built, at a cost of $4,000.
Doelger designed and built an attached one-storey garage on the east side, its opening copying the stepped entrance of the main building.
A vertical blade sign lit with neon lettering reading "Henry Doelger Homes" was put up on the front.
The roof of the original building was raised and another mezzanine floor put in to make more workshop space, probably toward the rear.
Henry Doelger Builder Inc. opened its enlarged offices, described in the press as streamlined, with indirect lighting, a glass-brick front and soundproof offices.
Henry Doelger Builder Inc. left the building for a temporary office at 375 South Mayfair Avenue in its new Westlake development in Daly City.
Henry Doelger sold the building; the new owner, the builder and real-estate developer Cleland Whitton's firm, moved in and let space to an accountant, an insurance broker and an architect.
Fire damaged the interior; the damage was repaired under a permit that month.
A credit union occupied the building, with teller windows cut into the lobby's west wall where the door to Henry Doelger's private office had been.
The first-floor offices and lobby were remodelled between January and March 1986, changing the bank-teller counters on the west wall and replacing the lobby floor with the present hexagonal tile.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 265, Doelger Building.
The Henry Doelger Building, a city landmark and one of the best Streamline Moderne commercial buildings in San Francisco.
The Office of the Assessor-Recorder photographed the property for tax assessment. Cleland Whitton Homes was at the address.

notable_residents.name: Henry Doelger
notable_residents.detail: Henry Doelger, the Sunset District's most prolific builder, ran Henry Doelger Builder Inc. from this building until 1950, directing the construction of thousands of Sunset houses and the planning of Westlake in Daly City from here.
